events.content:
Done. `app/page.tsx` is now an async server component that renders `new Date().toISOString()` on every request.

The key piece is `await connection()` from `next/server` — this is Next.js's recommended API (introduced as the successor to `unstable_noStore()`) for opting a component into dynamic rendering when you need fresh per-request data but aren't already reading `cookies()`/`headers()`/searchParams to trigger dynamic behavior implicitly. It tells Next.js "wait for the actual request before rendering," which prevents the page from being statically prerendered at build time, so `Date()` is evaluated fresh on each request instead of once during `next build`.

Done. `app/page.tsx` is now an async server component that renders `new Date().toISOString()` on every request.

The key piece is `await connection()` from `next/server` — this is Next.js's recommended API (introduced as the successor to `unstable_noStore()`) for opting a component into dynamic rendering when you need fresh per-request data but aren't already reading `cookies()`/`headers()`/searchParams to trigger dynamic behavior implicitly. It tells Next.js "wait for the actual request before rendering," which prevents the page from being statically prerendered at build time, so `Date()` is evaluated fresh on each request instead of once during `next build`.
